                                                               Who we are
                                                               Perenti is an Australian Securities Exchange listed, diversified
                                                               mining services group with expertise in contract mining, drilling
                                                               and mining services and technology solutions. Headquartered
                                                               in Perth, we operate across four continents and employ 10,000
                                                               people. We aim to be the safest and most productive in the
                                                               industry, unlocking enduring value and certainty for our people,
                                                               clients, communities and shareholders.

                                                               About this report
                                                               This Annual Report is a summary of Perenti and our
                                                               operations, activities and financial position as at 30 June
                                                               2026. All dollar figures are expressed in Australian dollars
                                                               unless otherwise stated.

                        Dividends
                        On 21 August 2026, the directors have determined the payment of an unfranked dividend
                        of 4.5 cents per fully paid share to be paid on 28 October 2026, with a record date of
                        14 October 2026. The Company’s Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP) is currently suspended
                        until further notice.

                        The 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM) of Perenti Limited will be held on 16 October 2026.

                        Strategically managing our portfolio of businesses
                        Active portfolio management remains a key lever in delivering
                        long-term value creation through the cycle. We continue to
                        take a disciplined approach to capital allocation, investing in
                        businesses where we hold strong competitive advantages while
                        divesting assets that no longer align with our strategic priorities.
                        Over the past decade, Perenti has deliberately reshaped its
                        portfolio to build globally scaled mining services businesses.
                        The acquisitions of Barminco and DDH1 strengthened our
                        underground mining and drilling capabilities respectively,
                        creating leading global positions in attractive market segments.
                        At the same time, we have exited non-core businesses
                        demonstrating our commitment to focusing capital on areas
                        of highest strategic value.
                        This approach was recently further demonstrated through
                        the divestment of BTP. Following a disciplined portfolio review,
                        Perenti agreed to sell BTP for total consideration of $100 million,
                        comprising an initial $80 million payment and a deferred
                        $20 million payment. The transaction will further enhance group
                        financial capacity and supports recycling of capital into higher-
                        returning opportunities, including recent contract
                        awards and future growth initiatives.
                        In addition, and also subsequent to year end, AMS agreed an
                        orderly transition at AngloGold Ashanti’s Iduapriem Gold Mine
                        in Ghana, extending services while agreeing the sale of its on-
                        site fleet for expected proceeds of $30-40 million. Together,
                        these actions are unlocking capital and strengthening our ability
                        to invest in future growth opportunities across Australia, North
                        America and Africa.

                                                                                             Recognising outstanding safety leaders
                                                                                             Introduced in late 2024, Perenti's Outstanding Safety Leaders
                                                                                             Program recognises frontline individuals and teams who
                                                                                             demonstrate exceptional safety leadership and a
                                                                                             commitment to preventing harm across our operations.
                                                                                             Since launch, the quarterly program has recognised more
                                                                                             than 20 leaders from Contract Mining, Drilling Services and
                                                                                             Mining Services for contributions ranging from critical risk
                                                                                             management and innovation to coaching, mentoring and
                                                                                             speaking up for safety. By celebrating positive safety
                                                                                             behaviours and sharing success stories, the program helps
                                                                                             strengthen leadership capability and reinforce a strong safety
                                                                                             culture across the Group.

                                                                                 Building leadership capability
                                                                                 In FY26, Perenti launched its Management Development
                                                                                 Program, a 12-month leadership initiative delivered in
                                                                                 partnership with the UNSW Australian Graduate School of
                                                                                 Management. The program forms part of the expanding suite
                                                                                 of offerings within Perenti’s Leadership Academy. The inaugural
                                                                                 cohort brought together 15 leaders from across the Group’s
                                                                                 businesses and geographies to strengthen strategic thinking,
                                                                                 commercial acumen and leadership capability.
                                                                                 Combining executive education, coaching, 360-degree
                                                                                 feedback and practical business projects, the program is
                                                                                 designed to build a strong pipeline of future leaders and support
                                                                                 the delivery of Perenti's strategy. Participants graduate with a
                                                                                 Graduate Certificate and have the opportunity to continue their
                                                                                 studies towards an MBA.

                        demonstrate our ability to grow while maintaining
                        a disciplined approach to execution and winning work.
                        Subsequent to year end, we secured a six-month extension
                        for African Mining Services at Iduapriem while agreeing the
                        sale of the mining fleet to AngloGold Ashanti as part of an
                        orderly transition plan due to surface mining localisation.




                                                                                         Critical Risk Refresh: Strengthening the controls that
                                                                                         save lives
                                                                                         Contract Mining made significant progress on its Critical Risk
                                                                                         Management refresh during the year, strengthening the
                                                                                         prevention of fatal incidents. Driven by learnings from
                                                                                         fatalities, significant potential incidents and extensive
                                                                                         frontline feedback, the program expanded the division’s
                                                                                         Critical Risks from 12 to 15 and introduced updated
                                                                                         Standards, verification systems and safety tools based on
                                                                                         credible fatality scenarios identified through bowtie risk
                                                                                         assessments.
                                                                                         The refresh focused on ensuring critical controls are
                                                                                         consistently understood, verified and applied across all
                                                                                         operations. New visual standards, including refreshed critical
                                                                                         risk icons and signage, were introduced to create a single,
                                                                                         globally consistent approach across Contract Mining’s
                                                                                         operations and joint ventures.
                                                                                         At the frontline, the refresh transformed how critical controls
                                                                                         are verified before work begins. New and updated tools,
                                                                                         including Start Work In Control, CheckMate and CheckIns,
                                                                                         were developed through extensive consultation with
                                                                                         employees across multiple sites and regions. The tools are
                                                                                         designed to move teams beyond compliance-based
                                                                                         processes, strengthening hazard identification, verification of
                                                                                         critical controls and meaningful safety conversations that
                                                                                         help prevent serious incidents.
                                                                                         By strengthening how critical risks are identified, managed
                                                                                         and discussed, the refresh represents an important step in
                                                                                         embedding a proactive safety culture and supporting
                                                                                         Contract Mining’s commitment to ensuring every person
                                                                                         returns home safely.

                                                                                             One team, multiple capabilities – Creating value at
                                                                                             Regis Resources
                                                                                             Regis Resources' Duketon Operations demonstrates the
                                                                                             strength of Perenti's integrated mining services model, with
                                                                                             multiple businesses working together to deliver a seamless
                                                                                             solution across the mining value chain.
                                                                                             At the site, Strike Drilling provides reverse circulation drilling,
                                                                                             DDH1 Drilling delivers diamond drilling services, and
                                                                                             Barminco runs underground mining operations. Together,
                                                                                             these businesses combine specialist expertise with a shared
                                                                                             commitment to safety, operational excellence and customer
                                                                                             service.
                                                                                             By leveraging the complementary capabilities of multiple
                                                                                             Perenti businesses, Regis benefits from a coordinated
                                                                                             approach that improves communication, simplifies project
                                                                                             delivery and creates operational efficiencies. Shared safety
                                                                                             systems, aligned planning processes and strong
                                                                                             collaboration between site teams enable faster problem
                                                                                             solving and consistent execution, while providing the
                                                                                             flexibility to respond to changing operational requirements.
                                                                                             The partnership also reflects the strength of long-term
                                                                                             relationships built on trust and performance. As drilling and
                                                                                             contract mining requirements continue to evolve, Perenti's
                                                                                             integrated model positions the Group to deliver greater
                                                                                             value than any single service provider could achieve alone.
                                                                                             This collaboration exemplifies the Group's Smarter together
                                                                                             philosophy, demonstrating how combining expertise across
                                                                                             businesses creates safer operations, stronger client
                                                                                             partnerships and better outcomes for everyone involved.

                        Health and wellbeing
                        Perenti recognises that protecting the health and wellbeing of
                        our workforce is essential to our business and the communities
                        we operate in. We are committed to preventing work-related
                        illnesses and providing services that support the physical and
                        psychological wellbeing of all employees and contractors.
                        Occupational health services at Perenti include pre-employment
                        medicals, periodic health assessments and return-to-work
                        programs. We conduct respiratory screening, noise monitoring
                        and vibration assessments, particularly for people in roles where
                        there is the potential for exposure to atmospheric contaminants
                        or physical agents (e.g. noise) such as underground mining or
                        drilling. We have suitably qualified people available at all work
                        locations to provide immediate treatment and care for our
                        people. Medivac procedures are in place where required.
                        Each division is responsible for implementing health
                        management plans aligned with local legislation, client
                        requirements and Perenti’s Group standards. In FY26,
                        we continued to implement:
                        ▪    Health risk assessments across sites with a focus on
                             occupational hygiene, psychosocial hazards and
                             psychological safety.
                        ▪    Training to raise awareness of key health risks, including
                             fatigue, hydration, mental health, psychosocial hazards,
                             psychological safety, PPE use and hygiene practices.
                        ▪    Proactive leader engagement for recognising health-related
                             risks in the field.
                        In addition to health management plans, we are also
                        investigating opportunities to reduce health risks. Key initiatives
                        for FY26 included:
                        ▪    Contract Mining continued to identify the functional              BTP’s mobile fume extraction unit.
                             specifications required to further enhance our fatigue
                             monitoring technology for global rollout. A rigorous process
                             was undertaken to find a commercial platform that
                             enhances efficiencies, improves safety and supports better
                             decision-making. Deployment of the OPTIX Fatigue
                             Management System across Australian operations is well
                             progressed, informed by learnings from the initial
                             deployment in Africa by our Underground Mining Alliance
                             (UMA) joint venture partnership.

                                                                                             Engineering solution for high-risk maintenance
                                                                                             activity
                                                                                             The use of pulling/pressing rods is a high-risk maintenance
                                                                                             activity that uses a hydraulic cylinder to remove seized
                                                                                             components from mobile equipment. If rod and cylinder
                                                                                             capacities are mismatched the rods can become overloaded,
                                                                                             break, and become potentially lethal projectiles.
                                                                                             This has been an industry challenge for a long time and
                                                                                             controls put in place have been largely administration based.
                                                                                             To help solve this industry challenge, BTP partnered with the
                                                                                             Robotics Engineering Department at the University of
                                                                                             Technology, Sydney. By partnering with non-industry people,
                                                                                             they were able to look at the project independently and have
                                                                                             developed a solution that is currently being trialled as a
                                                                                             working prototype.




For personal use only
                                                                                             The working prototype integrates load sensors along with
                                                                                             system identification of critical components (rod & hydraulic
                                                                                             cylinder) that are confirmed via a Radio Frequency
                                                                                             Identification (RFID) scanning system. The tooling will not
                                                                                             operate if the components do not have an RFID code and
                                                                                             additionally, the force applied is limited to the load rating of
                                                                                             the weakest component.

                                                                                              Psychosocial safety learning event
                                                                                              In February 2026, employees from Perenti’s Perth based teams
                                                                                              along with some of our project managers were invited to a
                                                                                              unique learning event exploring psychosocial safety. A live
                                                                                              industrial theatre workshop delivered an interactive case study,
                                                                                              centred around a WorkSafe inspector sent to investigate a
                                                                                              windrow collision on a mine site. While it appeared to be
                                                                                              straightforward, through interviews and conversations with
                                                                                              people on site, it became clear that there was more to the story.
                                                                                              Delivered in three acts, the play explored themes of
                                                                                              psychosocial safety, workplace culture, speaking up,
                                                                                              leadership, risk assessment and safety culture. During intervals,
                                                                                              the audience were given time to discuss and reflect on what
                                                                                              they had heard, and review the psychosocial workplace
                                                                                              hazards they had identified.




For personal use only
                                                                                              It was a thought provoking and insightful experience.
                                                                                              The production was developed by ACT Australia and New
                                                                                              Zealand with funding from the Mental Awareness, Respect and
                                                                                              Safety (MARS) Program, which is a government led initiative in
                                                                                              Western Australia aimed at improving the health, safety and
                                                                                              wellbeing of employees in the mining industry.

                                                                                            Building Perenti’s future leaders
                                                                                            In FY26, Perenti launched its Management Development
                                                                                            Program, a 12-month leadership initiative developed in
                                                                                            collaboration with the University of New South Wales Australian
                                                                                            Graduate School of Management. The inaugural cohort,
                                                                                            launched in August 2025, brought together 15 leaders from
                                                                                            across the Group’s operational, functional and regional teams
                                                                                            to strengthen strategic capability, operational excellence and
                                                                                            adaptive leadership across the business.
                                                                                            The program combines immersive residential learning,
                                                                                            360-degree feedback, coaching and practical business
                                                                                            challenge projects aligned with Perenti’s Strategy. By investing
                                                                                            in leadership capability, the program supports a stronger and
                                                                                            more agile leadership pipeline, helping participants broaden
                                                                                            their enterprise perspective, improve financial and risk
                                                                                            discipline, and lead in a way that reflects The Perenti Way.
                                                                                            On completion, a graduate certificate will be awarded and
                                                                                            enables participants the option to continue on to complete
                                                                                            a Master of Business Administration.

                                                                                            BTP surpasses 90% workforce competency and
                                                                                            compliance milestone
                                                                                            In FY26, BTP achieved a key safety and capability milestone,
                                                                                            reaching more than 90% overall competency and compliance
                                                                                            across its operational workforce. The result reflects the
                                                                                            successful delivery of the competency uplift program
                                                                                            introduced in 2024, including mandatory and supplementary
                                                                                            Verification of Competency assessments, enhanced induction
                                                                                            pathways and BTP’s Assessor Development Program. Across
                                                                                            WA, NSW and Queensland, employees completed 3,720 theory
                                                                                            and practical VoC assessments and 13,234 training and
                                                                                            compliance activities.
                                                                                            The program has improved consistency in assessment,
                                                                                            increased awareness of workplace risks and hazards, and
                                                                                            helped ensure BTP’s workforce continues to meet legislative
                                                                                            and client requirements. A strong in-house assessor network
                                                                                            has also strengthened local ownership of competency,
                                                                                            reduced training bottlenecks and supported employees to
                                                                                            progress from theory to demonstrated capability. BTP will
                                                                                            continue to invest in assessor development, system
                                                                                            improvements and targeted training to maintain current
                                                                                            competencies and support a safer, more capable workforce.

                        Waste
                        Responsible waste management promotes environmental
                        sustainability by diverting waste from landfill, reducing pollution
                        and promoting a circular economy. We adhere to waste
                        management requirements on our client sites and additionally
                        work to implement recycling and circular economy initiatives
                        where we have control and influence at our own facilities.
                        We also continue to collect waste-related data to monitor
                        performance and identify future improvement opportunities.

                        Water stewardship
                        We recognise that water is essential for sustaining life and
                        ecosystems and responsible management is imperative to our
                        operations. As a mining services company, our water is
                        generally supplied by our clients at the sites where we work.
                        Water used in our offices and workshops is generally sourced
                        from municipal or third-party water providers.
                        We are committed to supporting our clients with their site
                        water conservation strategies and minimise our consumption,

                             Contributing to the long-term prosperity of the
                             Ghanzi region in Botswana
                             AMS was proud to sponsor the 2025 Ghanzi Agricultural
                             Show, which took place from 21-28 July in Ghanzi,
                             Botswana – approximately 70km from our operations
                             at Sandfire’s Motheo copper mine. The annual show is a
                             flagship event for Ghanzi, attracting over 500 exhibitors
                             and 10,000 attendees while playing a pivotal role in
                             fostering rural economic development and agricultural
                             excellence in Botswana. This year’s show saw major
                             upgrades to the exhibition grounds, including new fencing,
                             stalls, restrooms, and water infrastructure – all designed to
                             ensure long-term sustainability and improved functionality
                             of the venue. The show was also strongly focused on
                             improving community welfare beyond the event.
                             AMS’ sponsorship of the Ghanzi Agricultural Show
                             demonstrates our commitment to sustainable community
                             development. Through our sponsorship of the event, we
                             have not only contributed to Botswana’s agricultural sector,
                             but also strengthened community resilience and contribute
                             to the long-term prosperity of the Ghanzi region.

                        Anti-bribery and anti-corruption                                    Industry association memberships
                        Perenti maintains a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and          Perenti, or its operating businesses, are members of industry
                        corruption across all areas of its global operations. Our ABAC      associations or organisations including:
                        Policy outlines the Group’s firm commitment to ethical conduct
                        and responsible business practices. This is further supported by
                        our Compliance Group Standard and ABAC Standard, which
                        specifies mandatory ABAC requirements for employees,
                        contractors and suppliers.
                        All material breaches of the ABAC Policy are required to be
                        reported to the Board and Audit and Risk Committee. No material
                        breaches of the ABAC Policy were reported in FY26.
                        In FY26, Perenti continued to implement and reinforce its ABAC
                        controls through training, monitoring and compliance reviews.
                        All employees are required to complete online Code of Conduct
                        training, and employees in higher-risk roles, such as supervisors
                        and those involved in procurement or commercial negotiations,
                        are required to complete a tailored ABAC training module.
                        As per the ABAC Policy, all business divisions maintain gift and
                        hospitality registers, managed by designated employees, to




For personal use only
                        ensure transparency and accountability in business interactions.
                        During FY26, the Chief Corporate Services Officer (CCSO) and
                        the Perenti Corporate Legal and Compliance functions had
                        oversight over ABAC governance, including maintaining a register
                        of incidents and overseeing corrective actions, where applicable.
                        From 1 June 2026, the Chief Financial Officer replaced the role
                        of the CCSO. The ABAC Policy is reviewed every two years to
                        ensure it remains aligned with evolving legal and ethical
                        standards.                                                          Our engagement with these organisations is consistent with the
                                                                                            Perenti Code of Conduct, and a detailed list of our industry
                        Human rights and modern slavery
                                                                                            associations is provided in the FY26 Databook.
                        At Perenti, we recognise that respecting and upholding human
                        rights is a fundamental responsibility of all businesses.
                        Our approach is guided by our Human Rights Policy and Code
                        of Conduct and is operationalised through employee training
                        and due diligence processes.
                        In FY26, we continued to strengthen human rights awareness
                        across our operations and supply chain. To support this, Contract
                        Mining’s Supply Team’s new digital onboarding platform includes
                        a supplier due diligence process. This platform streamlines
                        processes for onboarding, pre-qualification and ongoing
                        compliance management, enhancing procurement governance,
                        improving risk oversight and reinforcing our commitment to
                        addressing modern slavery and human rights obligations within
                        our supplier network.
                        Perenti did not conduct audits of its security contractor against
                        the Voluntary Principles on Security and Human Rights (VPSHR)
                        in FY26, as audits had been completed in the previous three
                        years. However, our Ghana-based security contractor delivered
                        VPSHR training to their workforce, as recommended in prior
                        audits. A reduction in our operational footprint in Burkina Faso
                        has meant that we now have a reduced reliance on security
                        contractors carrying out monitoring and guarding activities at
                        the Ouagadougou based offices.
                        In FY26, we continued to implement our modern slavery
                        due diligence processes using onboarding surveys and
                        questionnaires. This included Drilling Services conducting a
                        modern slavery survey of its long-term contractors.
                        Our FY25 Modern Slavery Statement can be viewed at
                        perenti.com/sustainability/. An updated Modern Slavery
                        Statement for FY26 will be prepared and published in
                        accordance with the relevant legislation for the jurisdictions
                        in which we operate.

                        4.1.       Climate-related risks and opportunities
                        Perenti initially identified climate-related risks and opportunities
                        across the Group and its value chain through internal stakeholder
                        engagement, review of past climate events, and support from an
                        external adviser, then refined the assessment to focus on those
                        risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to
                        affect Perenti’s prospects, informing the subsequent financial
                        quantification and scenario analysis. Each climate-related risk and
                        opportunity was assessed using Perenti's enterprise risk
                        management matrix considering both consequence and
                        likelihood across three time horizons.

                        3. Extreme heat — workforce and underground ventilation impacts (Acute)
                        Category: Physical      Value chain exposure: Core Operations                                  Time horizon: Long term
                        Potential impacts       Extreme heat may adversely affect workforce health, productivity and operating efficiency across
                        on our business         Perenti’s operations, with potential flow-through impacts to costs and revenue. Prolonged high
                        model and value         temperatures can require workforce adjustments, constrain underground ventilation performance,
                        chain                   reduce equipment efficiency in surface operations and increase cooling and energy demands.
                        Current and             Perenti manages exposure to extreme heat through a combination of operational, contractual and
                        ongoing responses       critical risk controls. Operations are predominantly mechanised and supported by mine design and
                                                scheduling that allows activities to be relocated to cooler underground areas where feasible,
                                                together with site-level heat risk assessments and critical controls for thermal extremes. Contractual
                                                mechanisms and measures such as workshop cooling and the use of dedicated cooling stations may

                        Monitoring              Occurs through site-level heat risk assessments, climate and weather forecasting, Critical risk

                        4. Operational disruptions due to extreme weather events (Acute)
                        Category: Physical      Value chain exposure: Core Operations                                        Time horizon: Short - long-term
                        Potential impacts on    Extreme weather events may disrupt Perenti’s operations across its divisions, affecting workforce health and
                        our business model      safety, operational continuity and project delivery. This may increase the chance of incidents and result in
                        and value chain         increased maintenance and repair costs and lost revenue from operational disruptions.
                                                Drilling Services: Bushfires and severe storms/cyclones may result in site evacuations or shutdowns, damage to
                                                equipment, reducing productivity and delaying drilling operations.
                                                Contract Mining: Operational disruption from loss of site access caused by heavy precipitation, causing
                                                inundated or damaged mine roads, flooded river crossings, and delays to workforce mobilisation. Severe storms
                                                and cyclones may damage equipment and mine infrastructure, which may increase operating costs associated
                                                with equipment damage and affecting Perenti’s ability to operate client sites.
                                                Mining and Technology Services: Operational disruption from damage to transport and logistics infrastructure
                                                may limit the delivery of equipment, parts and other supplies.
                        Current and             Perenti manages exposure through existing operational and contractual controls, including weather and
                        ongoing responses       lightning monitoring, site-level controls (such as fire breaks and water diversion bunds, groundwater pumping
                                                regimes), and increased pre-season stockholding of critical spares. These measures reduce immediate
                                                operational impacts and are effective in managing localised disruptions in the short to medium term. However,
                                                as extreme weather events are projected to become more frequent and intense, residual operational disruption
                                                is expected to persist in the long-term despite existing controls.
                        Monitoring              Occurs through ongoing site-level weather and hazard monitoring, including cyclone, bushfire and severe
                                                storm alerts, supported by established warning, escalation and evacuation procedures.

                        Appendix B: Definition of terms
                        Term                                   Definition
                        Climate-related risks and              Risks and opportunities arising from climate change that could reasonably be expected to affect the Group’s prospects, strategy, business
                        opportunities                          model, value chain, financial position, performance or cash flows.
                        Climate resilience                     The Group’s capacity to adapt its strategy and business model under different climate scenarios, including identified sources of resilience
                                                               and key limitations/uncertainties.
                        Climate-related matters working        The group comprises representatives from Perenti’s Risk, Finance, Investor Relations, Governance, Insurance, Corporate Strategy, divisional
                        group                                  sustainability team, and the Corporate Sustainability team. The group provides cross-functional input to support climate-related risk
                                                               assessment, strategy development, and disclosure activities across the business.
                        GreenPower                             A government-managed program in Australia that lets households and businesses buy certified renewable energy through their regular
                                                               electricity retailer.
                        LGCs                                   A LGC represents 1 megawatt-hour (MWh) of electricity generated from an eligible renewable energy source. LGCs contribute to the
                                                               market-based Scope 2 calculation.
                        Internal carbon pricing                A formal internal carbon price, fee, or shadow price used in decision-making or scenario analysis.
                        Materiality (climate-related           The basis used to determine which climate-related information is relevant to users, applying judgement and thresholds (financial,
                        disclosures)                           reputational and safety) to decide what is material or required for disclosure.
                        Operational control (GHG boundary) Approach under which the Group reports 100% of Scope 1 and 2 emissions from facilities over which it has operational control (e.g., offices,
                                                           workshops, warehouses, accommodation, training centres), excluding client mine/exploration sites where it lacks authority to introduce
                                                           operating policies.
                        Reporting boundary                     The entities, assets and operations included in this report, aligned with the consolidated financial statements and controlled entities
                                                               boundary.




For personal use only
                        Residual risk rating                   Risk rating assessed after considering existing controls, mapped using the enterprise 5×5 risk matrix (e.g., Low/Medium/High/Very High).
                        Scenario analysis                      Structured approach used to assess resilience and the range of potential impacts under multiple plausible climate futures, using externally
                                                               sourced SSP/NGFS scenarios with qualitative and selective quantitative analysis.
                        Scope 1 emissions                      Direct greenhouse gas emissions from combustion of hydrocarbons at facilities under Perenti’s operational control (diesel, unleaded petrol,
                                                               LPG, acetylene, oils/greases etc.).
                        Scope 2 emissions (location-based)     Indirect emissions from purchased electricity calculated using grid-average emission factors for relevant regions.
                        Scope 2 emissions (market-based)       Supplementary Scope 2 calculation reflecting renewable electricity procurement (e.g., GreenPower supported by LGCs), treated as zero-
                                                               emissions electricity for that calculation.
                        Scope 3 emissions                      Other indirect emissions occurring in the value chain, calculated for relevant categories using spend based, activity based and hybrid
                                                               estimation methods depending on data availability.
                        Time horizons (short/medium/long)      Planning horizons used consistently across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics/targets sections: short-term to 2027,
                                                               medium-term to 2030, long-term to 2050.
                        Transition relief (comparatives)       First-year relief applied for comparative information disclosure under AASB S2 Appendix C paragraph C3, as stated in the report.

                        Remuneration Report




                                                                                           Andrea Sutton

                        Dear Fellow Shareholders,
                        On behalf of the Board, I am pleased to present Perenti’s Remuneration Report for the financial year ending 30 June 2026.
                        This report details our remuneration framework and outcomes for FY26.




For personal use only
                        This is my first Remuneration Report as Chair of the People and Remuneration Committee (Committee) of the Board of Perenti.
                        On behalf of the Board, I would like to acknowledge and thank Timothy Longstaff, who retired from the Board during the year for
                        his outstanding leadership as Chair of the Committee, and his significant contribution to Perenti throughout his tenure.
                        A year in review
                        FY26 was a year of disciplined execution, portfolio optimisation and leadership transition for Perenti. The Group continued to
                        strengthen its foundations for sustainable future growth while maintaining a steadfast focus on safety, operational excellence and
                        long-term shareholder value creation. While the year included a number of operational and market challenges, including the
                        conclusion of certain contracts and ongoing competitive pressures across parts of the portfolio, the Group responded through
                        disciplined project selection, cost management and a continued focus on the quality and sustainability of future earnings.
                        Key business highlights from the year include:
                        •    Continued progress in safety performance, supported by         •   Secured a number of significant new contracts and
                             investment in critical controls, leadership capability and         extensions, including the Bellevue Gold Project
                             safe and respectful workplace initiatives.                         underground contract, the Duketon contract extension,
                        •    Delivery of a strong financial performance, characterised          the Dalgaranga project and most recently the Four Mile
                             by resilient earnings, margin improvement and disciplined          Project in the United States. These wins partially offset the
                             cost management, including underlying EBIT(A) increasing           conclusion of several existing contracts and further
                             to $339.7 million (up 1.9%) and underlying NPAT(A)                 strengthened the quality, geographic diversity and
                             increasing by 7.6%, reflecting improved earnings quality           duration of future earnings.
                             and margin expansion.                                          •   Continued to actively reshape the portfolio through
                        •    Strong cash flow generation, including adjusted free cash          disciplined project selection, responding to changing
                             flow of $181.6 million, and conservative leverage,                 market conditions and exiting lower-return or
                             reflecting the Group’s continued focus on capital                  underperforming operations. While these decisions
                             discipline and balance sheet strength.                             reduced exposure to certain projects, they supported the
                        •    Ongoing returns to shareholders through dividends and              reallocation of capital toward higher-quality, higher-
                             share price appreciation, reflecting confidence in the             margin opportunities and a more resilient earnings profile

                             contract roll-offs and providing confidence in

                        The year also saw the successful execution of Board and executive leadership succession, including the appointment of new
                        Directors and the transition from former Managing Director and CEO Mark Norwell to Vanessa Torres as Managing Director and
                        CEO. We welcomed Gregory Walker and Vincent Nicoletti to the Board following the retirement of Alexandra Atkins and Timothy
                        Longstaff. We also farewelled Mark Norwell after eight years of dedicated service as Managing Director and CEO and welcomed
                        Vanessa Torres, whose extensive global resources experience positions the Group well for its next phase of growth. Details of
                        these leadership transitions, including the remuneration arrangements applicable to Mark Norwell and Vanessa Torres, are outlined
                        in Section 3.
                        FY26 remuneration outcomes in summary
                        The Board remains committed to responsible, transparent remuneration practices that align leadership reward with business
                        performance and long-term shareholder interests. Consistent with this, executive remuneration outcomes for FY26 were closely
                        aligned with performance. Incentives rewarded delivery against financial and operational goals, while also reflecting outcomes in
                        safety and shareholder value.
                        Executive KMP were on average rewarded as follows under incentive plans:
                        • Short Term Incentive (STI) Plan (STIP) outcomes were 76.6% of maximum; and
                        • Long Term Incentive (LTI) Plan (LTIP) outcomes for the FY24 grant (assessed over FY24-26) were 47.5% of maximum.
                        Further detail can be found in Section 5.
                        ABN 95 009 211 474                                                                             Perenti Remuneration Report      97




                        Remuneration reviews
                        In FY26, the Board undertook its annual review of the market remuneration data for Executive KMP and undertook a review of
                        Board fees. Following detailed analysis and careful consideration, adjustments were made to ensure our approach remains aligned
                        with Perenti’s remuneration philosophy, principles, market benchmarks and long-term strategy.
                        Details of the changes made following these reviews can be found for the Executive KMP in Sections 4-7, and for Board fees in
                        Section 9.
                        Looking forward
                        Looking ahead to FY27, and following a review of remuneration and governance arrangements with the support of an external
                        adviser, the Board has approved a number of targeted enhancements to further strengthen alignment between remuneration
                        outcomes, business performance and long-term shareholder value creation. These changes include:
                            •    the introduction of a hybrid scorecard for the STIP, enabling both Group and Divisional performance to be assessed for
                                 Divisional participants;
                            •    increased STIP deferral requirements, with the Managing Director and CEO required to defer 50% of any award
                                 (previously 33%), and other Executive KMP required to defer 40% (up from 33%) into restricted equity; and
                            •    the introduction of a Minimum Shareholding Requirement (MSR) Policy with effect from 1 July 2026.
                        Together, these enhancements further reinforce Perenti's commitment to executive reward arrangements that support sustainable
                        performance, appropriate risk management and long-term shareholder alignment. Further details are provided in Section 10.




For personal use only
                        Broader work
                        Beyond remuneration, the Committee continued to focus on strengthening leadership capability and building organisational depth
                        across the Group. Key areas of focus included executive and leadership succession planning, talent development and initiatives to
                        support long-term organisational effectiveness and capability. The Committee also maintained a strong focus on leadership
                        continuity and succession, particularly during a year of Board and executive leadership transition.
                        A significant milestone during the year was the rollout of the Management Development Program, delivered in partnership with the
                        Australian Graduate School of Management at the University of New South Wales. The program is designed to enhance leadership
                        effectiveness, commercial decision-making and execution discipline across the Group’s operations. Together with ongoing
                        investment in succession planning, talent development and employee engagement initiatives, these programs support the
                        development of a capable, resilient and high-performing organisation positioned to deliver sustainable performance and long-
                        term shareholder value.
                        A message of thanks
                        Our achievements during FY26 would not have been possible without the dedication and commitment of our people. On behalf
                        of the Board, I extend our sincere thanks to Perenti’s approximately 10,000 strong global workforce across 12 countries for their
                        significant and ongoing contribution to our business, our clients, our communities and our stakeholders. In a year that brought
                        both opportunities and challenges, your commitment to safety, operational excellence and client service remained fundamental to
                        the value we create and the trust we earn. Through your efforts, Perenti has continued to strengthen its foundations and position
                        the Group for long-term success as we continue to collectively create enduring value and certainty.
                        As we look ahead, we remain focused on continuously improving our business, strengthening our performance and delivering
                        sustainable value for shareholders and other stakeholders.
                        Thank you for your ongoing support. We look forward to welcoming you to our 2026 Annual General Meeting.




                        Andrea Sutton

                        3            MD & CEO transition
                        a. Remuneration details for MD & CEO
                        As previously announced, Vanessa Torres’ remuneration arrangements, as the MD & CEO, are as follows:
                              •      Total Fixed Remuneration (TFR): $1,250,000
                              •      STIP opportunity: Target 80% of TFR | Maximum 120% of TFR (subject to a 50% deferral requirement)

                        b. Leaving arrangements for the Former MD & CEO
                        The Board acknowledges the significant contribution of the Former MD & CEO during his tenure, including his leadership of
                        Perenti's transformation into a more diversified, resilient and higher-performing business.
                        In determining the treatment of his cessation arrangements, the Board considered the relevant incentive plan rules, governance
                        principles, and the specific circumstances of the leadership transition. The Board determined that the treatment of outstanding
                        incentive awards appropriately recognised performance delivered during the relevant performance periods, while remaining
                        consistent with the applicable plan rules and the Company's remuneration framework.
                        Given the Former MD & CEO remains employed by Perenti and continues to support the business in a strategic advisory capacity
                        following his transition from the MD & CEO role, the treatment of outstanding incentive awards is as follows:
                              •      eligible to participate in the FY26 STIP (with any award subject to applicable deferral arrangements) and FY24 LTIP
                                     (subject to the original performance conditions and testing outcomes); and
                              •      forfeiture of all FY25 LTIP Performance Rights. The Former MD & CEO did not participate in the FY26 LTIP.
                        These arrangements remain subject to the Former MD & CEO continuing to satisfy the requirements of a "Good Leaver" under
                        the relevant plan rules. Any incentive awards that vest remain subject to the malus and clawback provisions described elsewhere
                        in this Report.

                        The Group continued to strengthen its safety foundations in FY26 through enhanced critical risk

                        against key lead indicators, including safety culture measures and Critical Control System
                        Verifications, reflected the continued embedding of our safety transformation plans across the
                        business. While injury performance remained below expectations, the Group made meaningful
                        progress in reinforcing a culture of safety, accountability and continuous improvement.

                        6        FY26 Executive KMP remuneration framework
                        The remuneration packages of Executive KMP are comprised of fixed and variable ‘at-risk’ remuneration that align leadership

                        Diagram 1: The remuneration mix for Perenti’s Executive KMP at target levels for FY26 is represented below.

                        Total Fixed Remuneration
                        Description         A competitive level of TFR is offered to attract and retain high quality and experienced Executive KMP.
                        Approach            TFR comprises all fixed remuneration, including statutory superannuation contributions.
                                                TFR is reviewed annually and upon promotion to ensure that it is market competitive. The Company
                                                targets the median of the relevant market. To remain market competitive and to attract and retain talent,
                                                TFR benchmarking recognises Perenti’s complexity beyond market capitalisation, including revenue,
                                                industry and geographic reach.
                                                If the statutory superannuation contribution is required to increase, the Executive KMP will have an equal
                                                reduction in base salary to ensure their TFR is unchanged.
                        Changes for FY26        Effective 1 October 2025, the Board approved an increase in the President Contract Mining’s TFR to
                                                $1,000,000. This decision reflects market benchmarking, internal relativities and the importance of the
                                                role.
                        FY26 Short-term Incentive
                        Description         Executive KMP are eligible to participate in the annual STIP, which comprises a portion of their variable
                                            remuneration and is subject to performance measures. The STIP performance outcome is based on a
                                            balanced scorecard, which includes a mix of safety, financial and strategic measures.
                                                The MD & CEO did not participate in the FY26 STIP.
                        Performance period      Financial year
                        Opportunity             Target opportunity:   All Executive KMP: 67% of TFR
                                                Maximum opportunity: All Executive KMP: 100% of TFR
                        Award operation         The Executive KMP’s balanced scorecard comprises a mix of financial and non-financial measures. All
                                                measures have a threshold, target and stretch level of achievement. The weighting of each scorecard
                                                metric is then applied to its performance, with the total equalling the overall STIP outcome.

                        7        Remuneration governance
                        a. Roles and responsibilities
                        The roles and responsibilities of our Board, People and Remuneration Committee, management and external stakeholders and
                        advisors in relation to remuneration are outlined below.

                         Board                                                                                      External stakeholder engagement
                         Approves the overall Executive KMP remuneration framework, Executive KMP                   Consultation with proxy advisors and

                         People and Remuneration Committee
                         The Committee reviews and determines our remuneration framework annually
                         to ensure it remains aligned to business needs and meets our remuneration
                         principles.                                                                                External remuneration consultants
                                                                                                                    From time to time, the People and
                                                                                                                    Remuneration Committee may

                         information to assist with remuneration decisions and recommendations.
                         Communicates with external remuneration consultants to ensure the People
                         and Remuneration Committee has all the necessary information.

                        The purpose of the People and Remuneration Committee is to assist the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities regarding people
                        and remuneration. This includes overseeing that the Company has policies, frameworks and strategies which enable it to attract,
                        reward and retain an inclusive and diverse selection of directors, executives and employees that will create an engaged workplace
                        culture that contributes towards achieving positive outcomes for all stakeholders. The Committee also oversees succession.
                        For more information on the role of the Committee, please refer to its charter that is available on Perenti’s website.
                        Ernst and Young and Guerdon Associates were engaged during FY26 by the People and Remuneration Committee as external
                        remuneration advisors. This advice did not include any remuneration recommendations. The People and Remuneration
                        Committee is satisfied that the information provided was free from undue influence by any executive.

                        9            Non-executive Director remuneration
                        a. Non-executive Director fees
                        NED fees are set at a level which enables the attraction and retention of experienced and skilled Board members to ensure an
                        effective oversight role over the Company’s operations. Fee levels aim to reflect the demands which are made on, and the
                        responsibilities of, the directors. NED fees are reviewed periodically by the Board to ensure fee levels are appropriate and in-line
                        with the market.
                        The fee pool approved by shareholders at the FY23 Annual General Meeting is $1.4 million per annum. The current Perenti Board
                        fees are outlined below and are comfortably within this cap.

                        10       Changes for FY27
                        Following a review of Perenti's executive remuneration framework during FY26, the Board approved a number of enhancements
                        effective from 1 July 2026. These changes reflect Perenti's continued growth, recent inclusion in the ASX 200 and the Board's
                        commitment to maintaining remuneration arrangements that support long-term shareholder value creation, accountability and
                        contemporary governance practices.
                        a. Introduction of a MSR Policy
                        To further align executives and Non-Executive Directors with shareholder interests, the Board has introduced a Minimum
                        Shareholding Requirement Policy (Policy).
                        Under the Policy, participants are required to build and maintain a meaningful personal investment in Perenti through the
                        ownership of Perenti shares or share interests that are not subject to performance conditions.
                        The minimum holding requirements are:
                        •    NEDs - 100% of annual base NED fee (i.e. excluding Committee fees), exclusive of superannuation contributions, within
                             three years of appointment.
                        • MD & CEO and GEC Members - 100% of TFR within five years of appointment to the relevant position.
                        Participants covered by the policy will be required to retain shares acquired until their minimum holding requirement has been
                        satisfied, subject to limited exceptions such as taxation obligations or financial hardship.




For personal use only
                        b. Increased STIP deferral
                        To further strengthen executive alignment with long-term shareholder outcomes, the Board has increased the proportion of STIP
                        awards that will be delivered as deferred equity.

                                                      Portion of any award deferred as STI Rights
                                                     Previous approach            New approach
                        MD & CEO                             33%                       50%
                        Other GEC members                    33%                       40%

                        The deferral period remains unchanged at 12 months from the grant date.
                        Increasing the proportion of remuneration delivered in equity reinforces executive ownership, strengthens alignment with
                        shareholder experience and supports sustainable decision-making.
                        c. Introduction of a hybrid scorecard for the STIP
                        From FY27, the STIP framework for Divisional participants will be enhanced through the introduction of a hybrid scorecard
                        incorporating both Group and Divisional performance measures.
                        While Group performance will remain the primary driver of STIP outcomes, the Board recognises that a number of Perenti's
                        strategic growth opportunities are increasingly delivered through divisional execution. The revised scorecard is intended to
                        strengthen accountability and provide clearer line-of-sight between individual responsibilities and performance outcomes.
                        The FY27 scorecard will therefore include a balanced mix of:
                        •   Group performance measures;
                        •   Divisional performance measures; and
                        •   Continued focus on financial and safety outcomes.

                        The Board considers this approach better aligns reward outcomes with the drivers of value creation while maintaining appropriate
                        focus on overall Group performance.
                        Appropriate governance safeguards will continue to apply, including Board discretion to adjust outcomes where necessary to
                        reflect underlying performance, shareholder outcomes and safety or risk considerations.
                        Further details of the FY27 STIP framework, including performance measures and weightings, will be provided in the 2027
                        Remuneration Report.
                        d. FY27 LTIP strategic initiatives
                        Psychological safety has matured from a targeted transformation initiative into an embedded element of how the Group operates
                        and leads its people. While it remains a key priority, alongside all aspects of safety performance, and continues to be assessed
                        under outstanding FY25 and FY26 LTIP awards, the FY27 strategic initiatives have been refreshed to reflect the Group's evolving
                        strategic priorities and long-term growth ambitions.
                        The FY27 LTIP introduces measures focused on expanding Perenti's North American business and progressing the development of
                        a meaningful third pillar of earnings for the Group. These objectives support the Group's focus on broadening growth
                        opportunities, diversifying earnings streams and strengthening resilience over the long-term.
                        Consistent with the purpose of the LTIP, these measures have been designed to be appropriately challenging and require sustained
                        leadership focus, strategic execution and organisational capability to deliver. They are intended to align executive reward with the
                        successful execution of the Group's strategy and the creation of sustainable long-term shareholder value.
                        Further detail of the measures will be provided in the Notice of Meeting for the 2026 Annual General Meeting and subsequently in
                        the 2027 Remuneration Report.
